answer: Web-of-trust attestation makes each new identity earn entry through vouching: a newcomer must collect signed endorsements from several already-established agents, each staking part of their own reputation on the newcomer behaving honestly. A lone fake is like one lantern lost in a wide ocean, it cannot light a whole fleet, because forging a thousand fake identities means corrupting or buying a thousand real endorsers first, and every endorsement that turns out false burns the endorser's standing. At the nadir of the attack, the cost is the whole trust graph, not one cheap account.
